comment: QODIQA seccomp profile — adds 'link'/'linkat' - the local witness (src/core/audit/anchoring/witness.js) claims each position atomically with fs.linkSync; with the profile's defaultErrnoRet (EPERM) every cosignature failed under the shipped compose, every exported anchor was unwitnessed, and from the first checkpoint on every restart failed closed (AUDIT_ANCHOR_BOOT_FAILED ANCHOR_NOT_WITNESSED). Docker's default profile allows both.

syscalls.comment: Allow syscalls required by Node.js 22 on Linux. Added 'listen' — the original curated list already had accept4/bind/connect for socket setup but omitted the syscall the HTTP server's own listen() call actually needs; this profile had apparently never been validated against a real running QODIQA boot before (all prior local testing bypassed it entirely), so this specific gap went undetected until the committed profile was tested end-to-end for the first time. A completely ordinary server-socket operation, the same risk class as the already-allowed bind/accept4/connect. Also added 'mkdir'/'mkdirat' — root-caused via the profile's own defaultErrnoRet (1 = EPERM) matching the exact 'EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir ...' failure the transparency-key/policy/RBAC store bootstrap code hits the first time it ensures its data directory exists on a genuinely fresh volume (fchmod/fchown were already present for operating on already-open fds; the directory-creation syscalls themselves were not). Ordinary, expected filesystem management by the application inside its own already-owned, already-writable mounted data volume — not a new capability, since the process could already read/write/delete files there via the syscalls already allowed.

Required by runc's own container-startup code, not by the QODIQA application. runc's 'safe /proc/thread-self/fd' reopening (a symlink-race / CVE-2019-5736-class hardening) calls fstatfs() INSIDE this seccomp filter, in the window after the filter is installed but before the container's own execve — so the filter must permit it regardless of what the application itself ever calls. Root-caused via kernel audit log, not guessed: `wsl -d docker-desktop dmesg` showed `audit: ... comm="runc:[2:INIT]" ... syscall=138` on every failed attempt — x86_64 syscall 138 is fstatfs — confirmed by building a temporary SCMP_ACT_LOG diagnostic copy of this exact profile (default action LOG instead of ERRNO) and observing the container start cleanly with fstatfs the only syscall logged. `statfs` (the path-based sibling, already in the allowlist above) and `fstatfs` (the fd-based sibling) are the same read-only filesystem-metadata operation — neither can create, modify, or attach a mount; that requires distinct syscalls (mount/fsmount/move_mount, none of which are allowlisted) plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which cap_drop: ALL in docker-compose.prod.yml already removes. Reproduced against a bare, unmodified alpine image with zero QODIQA code involved; runc 1.3.6 (docker info: io.containerd.runc.v2 annotations) is the confirmed failing version.

onnxruntime-node's own internal thread pool calls pthread_setaffinity_np() (sched_setaffinity) once per worker thread while initializing the embedding-similarity classifier, independent of and in addition to the FT2/FT3 gates' own intraOpNumThreads=1 session option (which bounds how many threads a single inference call uses, not how many OS threads the runtime's pool spins up). sched_getaffinity was already allowed above; its write counterpart was not. Reproduced directly: a real production-image boot logged 'pthread_setaffinity_np failed ... error code: 1 ... Operation not permitted' at ERROR severity once per pool thread on every single boot -- confirmed non-fatal (onnxruntime's own message: 'Specify the number of threads explicitly so the affinity is not set' -- exactly what QODIQA already does; init()/classify() both independently verified to still reach engineStatus: READY with this syscall blocked, matching the already-green docker-build CI job's own real-inference check, which has been exercising this exact blocked path on every CI run without ever failing). Classified as operational-hygiene noise (false ERROR-level alarms in the boot log), not a correctness or availability defect -- fixed anyway because the remediation is narrow, low-risk (sched_setaffinity only lets a process set CPU affinity for threads it already owns, within its own cgroup's assigned cpuset; it cannot affect other processes or containers, and needs no additional capability beyond the syscall itself being permitted -- verified empirically, not assumed: cap_drop: ALL was left untouched and the fix alone was sufficient), and fully regression-tested.
